The final row must match publication and the captured revision; there must be no fallback to the stale snapshot. Within that same transaction I’ll preserve an existing embedding whose revision is newer, while allowing separate embedding versions to remain distinct.

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      # The provider is deliberately called outside the transaction. It may be slow,
      # and the document must be checked again after it returns.
      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      revision = snapshot.revision

      stored = Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id)
        next false unless current && current.tenant_id == tenant_id && current.published? && current.revision == revision

        embedding = Embedding.find_by(document_id: current.id, version: version)
        if embedding.nil?
          Embedding.create!(document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: revision,
                            version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector))
        elsif embedding.revision <= revision
          embedding.update!(tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: revision, vector: JSON.generate(vector))
        end

        true
      end

      stored ? :stored : :discarded
    end
  end
end
EOF

cat > test/regression_test.rb <<'EOF'
# frozen_string_literal: true

require_relative 'test_helper'

class EmbeddingJobRegressionTest < BenchmarkTest
  def call_for(document, tenant: 'a', version: 'v1', provider: ->(_body) { [1.0] })
    Knowledge::EmbeddingJob.new.call(document_id: document.id, tenant_id: tenant,
                                      version: version, provider: provider)
  end

  def test_discards_when_document_changes_while_provider_runs
    document = document(revision: 3)
    provider = lambda do |_body|
      document.update!(revision: 4)
      [1.0]
    end

    assert_equal :discarded, call_for(document, provider: provider)
    assert_empty Knowledge::Embedding.all
  end

  def test_discards_withdrawal_deletion_and_tenant_reassignment
    [
      ->(record) { record.update!(published: false) },
      ->(record) { record.destroy! },
      ->(record) { record.update!(tenant_id: 'b') }
    ].each do |change|
      document = document
      provider = lambda do |_body|
        change.call(document)
        [1.0]
      end

      assert_equal :discarded, call_for(document, provider: provider)
      assert_empty Knowledge::Embedding.all
    end
  end

  def test_does_not_overwrite_a_newer_embedding_and_versions_coexist
    document = document(revision: 1)
    Knowledge::Embedding.create!(document_id: document.id, tenant_id: 'a', revision: 2,
                                 version: 'v1', vector: JSON.generate([9.0]))

    assert_equal :stored, call_for(document, version: 'v1', provider: ->(_body) { [1.0] })
    assert_equal [9.0], JSON.parse(Knowledge::Embedding.find_by!(document_id: document.id, version: 'v1').vector)

    assert_equal :stored, call_for(document, version: 'v2', provider: ->(_body) { [2.0] })
    assert_equal %w[v1 v2], Knowledge::Embedding.where(document_id: document.id).order(:version).pluck(:version)
  end

  def test_provider_errors_propagate_without_writing
    document = document
    error = RuntimeError.new('provider failed')

    raised = assert_raises(RuntimeError) { call_for(document, provider: ->(_body) { raise error }) }

    assert_same error, raised
    assert_empty Knowledge::Embedding.all
  end

  def test_initially_unavailable_is_discarded_without_calling_provider
    document = document(published: false)
    called = false

    result = call_for(document, provider: ->(_body) { called = true; [1.0] })

    assert_equal :discarded, result
    refute called
    assert_empty Knowledge::Embedding.all
  end
end
EOF
